lānĕus , a, um, adj. id.,
I.woollen, of wool.
I. Lit.: “pallium,” Cic. N. D. 3, 34, 83 : “culcita ob oculos,” Plaut. Mil. 4, 4, 42 : “infula,” Verg. G. 3, 487 : thorax subuculae, Suet.
Aug. 82: “coma flaminis,” i. e. his woollen fillet, Stat. S. 5, 3, 183 : effigies, little woollen figures which were distributed at the Compitalia, acc. to Paul. ex Fest. p. 121 Müll.— “Prov.: dii irati laneos pedes habent,” i. e. the vengeance of the gods comes unperceived, Macr. S. 1, 8, 5 ; Petr. 44, v. 789.—
II. Transf.
A. Covered with a woolly sub stance, downy; of fruits: “pira corio laneo,” Plin. 15, 15, 16, § 55 (Jahn et Corrolana).—
B. Soft like wool, woolly: “lupus,” a kind of fish, Mart. 13, 89, 1 : “latusculum,” Cat. 25, 10 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
